overview: Joseon was Korea's longest-ruling dynasty, known for Neo-Confucian governance, scientific innovation and the creation of Hangul, one of the world's most scientific writing systems. The dynasty faced invasions but maintained cultural achievements until Japanese annexation.

items.text: King Sejong creates Hangul, the Korean alphabet, to promote literacy among common people.
Rain gauge invented, which predated European versions by two centuries.
Self-striking water clock and celestial globe created.
Astronomical observations and calendar reform under King Sejong.
Medical knowledge compiled in comprehensive pharmacopoeias.
White porcelain with blue underglaze designs becomes characteristic.
The Annals of the Joseon Dynasty compiled, one of the world's longest continuous historical records.
Neo-Confucianism becomes state orthodoxy, replacing Buddhism.
Civil service examinations based on Confucian classics select officials.
Admiral Yi Sun-sin uses turtle ships to repel Japanese invasions.
Gunpowder weapons and naval technology developed.
Hangul remains the Korean writing system today.
Neo-Confucian values shaped Korean society for centuries.

fall.text: Joseon was reorganized as the Korean Empire in 1897, though it was annexed by Japan in 1910.
